meaning: links a verb or adjective to how well, how much, or whether it can be done

senses.en: verb + 得 + comment on how it is done: 说得很好 'speaks very well'
adjective or verb + 得 + how far it goes: 累得不想动 'so tired I don't want to move'
verb + 得 + result = can manage it: 听得懂 'can understand' (negative 听不懂)

examples.en: You speak Chinese really well!
examples.analysis: 说得真好 'speak really well': verb, then 得, then the comment on how it is done. The object 汉语 comes before 说; you can also repeat the verb (说汉语说得真好), but 得 cannot follow the object directly.

examples.en: Did you sleep well last night?
examples.analysis: 睡得好 'sleep well': 得 links the verb 睡 to 好, the judgement of how the sleep went. 吗 makes it a question. A "no" puts 不 after 得: 睡得不好.

examples.en: I'm so tired I don't feel like eating.
examples.analysis: Here 得 follows an adjective, 累 'tired', and what comes after it shows how far the tiredness goes: 不想吃饭 'don't feel like eating'. English needs 'so … that'; Chinese gets the same meaning from 累得 + the result.

collocations.en: eat your fill; be really full

related.en: links a describer to a noun (我的书); 得 follows a verb or adjective
links a describer to the verb after it (慢慢地走)
to get, obtain (得到); a separate entry

meaning: to look like; to be like; to resemble

senses.en: to look like, take after (a person): 他像他爸爸
to be like, similar to; 像…一样 'like …, as … as …'
such as, like (before examples): 像北京、上海

examples.en: You really look like your mom!
examples.analysis: 像 takes the person you resemble as its object: 像 + 你妈妈. 长得 'in looks' narrows it to appearance; without it, 你真像你妈妈 can also mean you act or think like her.

examples.en: It's as hot as summer today.
examples.analysis: 像…一样 'like …': 像 brings in what it is compared with, 夏天 'summer', and 一样 'the same' closes the frame. The whole phrase follows 热得 and says how hot it is.

examples.en: That's not like you.
examples.analysis: 不 goes before 像 to deny the likeness: 这不像你 'this isn't like you'. People say it when someone acts out of character, kindly or as a gentle complaint. 啊 at the end adds feeling.

related.en: the same; pairs with 像 (像…一样)

meaning: so, this (much); like this, in this way

senses.en: so, this (before an adjective): 这么贵 'this expensive'
like this, in this way (before a verb): 这么做 'do it this way'

examples.en: It's so late. You're still up?
examples.analysis: 这么 + adjective points at something here and now: 这么晚了 'it's this late already'. 了 marks the new situation. The question after it, 还没睡 'still not asleep', is asked in surprise.

examples.en: How come it's so expensive?
examples.analysis: 怎么 here asks 'how come', not 'how', and 这么贵 'this expensive' is what the speaker is surprised by. A typical line at a shop or when the bill arrives.

examples.en: Don't say that.
examples.analysis: Before a verb, 这么 means 'like this, this way': 这么说 'say it like this'. 别这么说 'don't say that' pushes back on what someone just said: a person running themselves down, a gloomy remark, or an over-polite apology or thank-you.

collocations.en: put that way; so you mean …

related.en: so; like that (for what is farther away or already known)

meaning: it (for an animal or a thing)

senses.en: it: an animal (pets included) or a thing already mentioned
它们 (tāmen): they, for animals or things

examples.en: What's wrong with the dog? It keeps barking.
examples.analysis: 它 is the subject of the second sentence and points back to 狗 'dog'. 一直在 + verb says the barking has gone on without a break. 它, 他 and 她 all sound the same (tā); only the writing differs.

examples.en: What about your cat? How old is it now?
examples.analysis: 它 stands for 猫, named in the first question. 猫呢 here means 'and your cat?', picking up an earlier topic (with no context it means 'where is the cat?'). 几岁了 'how old now' uses the same words as for a child; 了 points to the age reached so far. Standard writing uses 它 for pets, even where English might say 'he' or 'she'.

examples.zh: 我的手机买了五年了，可是它还能用。
examples.en: I've had my phone for five years, but it still works.
examples.analysis: Here 它 stands for a thing, 手机 'phone'. Once the topic is clear, speakers often leave 它 out (可是还能用 is just as natural). 买了五年了 'bought five years ago, have had it five years'; 还能用 'can still be used' is the everyday way to say something still works.

meaning: for (someone's sake); because of, over (a cause)

senses.en: for, for the sake of (为 + person + verb or feeling): 为你高兴
because of, over (为 + cause + verb): 为这件事生气

examples.en: I'm so happy for you!
examples.analysis: 为 + person comes before the feeling: 为你 + 高兴 'happy for you'. English puts 'for you' at the end; Chinese puts the 为 phrase before the adjective or verb.

examples.en: Don't be angry about this anymore.
examples.analysis: 为 here gives the cause: 为这件事 'over this matter' sits before 生气 'be angry'. 别…了 here asks someone to stop a feeling that is already going on (别…了 can also talk someone out of something they are about to do, as in 别去了).

examples.en: This was made for you.
examples.analysis: 为你做 'made for you': 为 + person + verb names who it is for. 是…的 puts the focus on that part. In casual talk 给你做的 is just as common; 为 sounds a little more formal and stresses 'for your sake'.

related.en: for, to (the usual casual word: 给你做饭)

meaning: maybe, probably; possible; possibility

senses.en: may, might, probably (可能 + verb): 他可能不来
possible: 不可能 'impossible, no way'
possibility: 有可能 'there's a chance'

measure.note: as a noun: 还有一个可能 'there's one more possibility'

examples.en: He might not come after all.
examples.analysis: 可能 goes before the verb phrase to mark a guess: 他 + 可能 + 不来了. 了 at the end signals a change of plan: he was expected, now probably not.

examples.en: That's impossible!
examples.analysis: Here 可能 is an adjective, 'possible', and 不可能 is the everyday 'impossible' or 'no way'. People say it in disbelief at surprising news.

examples.en: Is there a chance it'll rain tomorrow?
examples.analysis: 可能 is a noun here, 'possibility': 有可能 'there is a chance'. 吗 turns it into a yes-no question, and 下雨 'rain' is what might happen. For a plain forecast question people also say 明天会下雨吗？

related.en: perhaps (an adverb only: it cannot mean 'possible' or 'a possibility')
will, likely to (明天会下雨 'it's going to rain tomorrow')

meaning: so, that (much); like that; well then, in that case

senses.en: so, that (before an adjective): 没那么难 'not that hard'
like that, in that way (before a verb): 那么做
well then, in that case (at the start of a sentence)

examples.en: It's not as hard as you say.
examples.analysis: A 没有 B 那么 + adjective = 'A is not as … as B'. Here A is left out and B is 你说的 'what you said', so the line plays down a worry: it isn't that hard.

examples.en: Well then, let's meet tomorrow.
examples.analysis: At the start of a sentence 那么 means 'well then, in that case': it wraps up what was said and moves to a decision. In casual talk 那 alone often does the same job (那我们明天见吧).

examples.en: He's so busy, he probably won't have time.
examples.analysis: 那么忙 'that busy': 那么 points to a degree both speakers already know about, here how busy he is. 这么 is used for what is close at hand; 那么 for what is farther away or being talked about.

related.en: so; like this (for what is close at hand)
then; in that case (casual, at the start of a sentence)

meaning: should, ought to; (a guess) should be, probably

senses.en: should, ought to: advice or duty (应该 + verb)
should be, probably: a confident guess: 他应该到了 'he should be there by now'

examples.en: You should get more rest.
examples.analysis: 应该 goes before the verb phrase to give advice: 应该 + 多休息. 多 before a verb means 'more', so 多休息 is 'rest more'. A typical line from a doctor or a worried friend.

examples.en: He should be there by now, right?
examples.analysis: Here 应该 is a guess, not advice: 'he has probably arrived by now'. 到了 says the arriving is done, and 吧 at the end asks the listener to agree.

examples.en: I shouldn't have said that.
examples.analysis: 不应该 'shouldn't'. The same words cover 'shouldn't' and 'shouldn't have'; here the context, something already said, makes it regret about one's own words. 这么说 'say it like this' refers to what the speaker just said.

collocations.en: it was the least I could do (reply to thanks)

related.en: maybe; a weaker guess than 应该

meaning: so; therefore; that's why

senses.en: so, therefore: brings in a result (often paired with 因为)
所以呢？ 'so? so what?': asks for the point or the consequence

examples.zh: 我有点儿累，所以先回家了。
examples.en: I'm a bit tired, so I'm going to head home ahead of you.
examples.analysis: 所以 opens the second clause and gives the result: tired, so going home. 先 'first, before the others' hints that the rest are staying; 了 announces the change of plan.

examples.zh: 因为下雨，所以我们没去。
examples.en: Because it rained, we didn't go.
examples.analysis: 因为…所以… is the 'because … so …' pair. English uses only one of the two words; Chinese often uses both. In quick speech either half can be dropped.

examples.en: So? What are you trying to say?
examples.analysis: 所以呢 on its own asks for the point or the consequence: 'so?' or 'so what?'. 呢 makes it a follow-up question. The tone can be curious or impatient, depending on the voice.

related.en: then, after that (a sequence, not a result)

meaning: not until, only then; only (a small amount); (emphatic) really

senses.en: not until, only then: later or harder than expected: 十点才起床
only, a mere (before a number): 才五块
(emphatic, 才…呢) really, definitely: 我才不去呢 'I'm definitely not going'

examples.en: He didn't get up until ten.
examples.analysis: 才 after a time phrase means 'not until': the event came later than expected. Compare 他六点就起床了, where 就 means 'as early as'. Sentences with this 才 usually do without 了.

examples.en: Why are you only getting here now?
examples.analysis: 才来 'only now arriving', said to someone who is late. 怎么 here means 'how come', so the line is a mild complaint rather than a real request for the reason.

examples.en: It's only twenty kuai. That's not expensive.
examples.analysis: Before a number, 才 means 'only, a mere': the speaker finds the amount small. 块钱 is the everyday way to say yuan. 不贵 'not expensive' spells out the judgement.

related.en: as early as; already (the opposite feeling of 才)

meaning: liang: a unit of weight, 50 grams (for food, tea, alcohol)

senses.en: liang: 50 grams; ten 两 make one 斤 (500 grams)
the portion unit in many noodle and dumpling shops: 二两饺子

examples.en: I'd like two liang (100 grams) of dumplings.
examples.analysis: 两 here is a unit of weight, 50 grams, not the number 'two'. The number before it is 二, not 两: 二两 is the set way to say it. Many dumpling and noodle shops sell portions this way.

examples.en: How much is this tea per liang?
examples.analysis: 多少钱 + 一 + measure word asks the price per unit: 'how much for one liang'. Tea is sold by weight, and many shops quote the price per 两 or per 斤, so this is a normal question at a tea shop.

examples.zh: 不用那么多，三两就够了。
examples.en: I don't need that much. Three liang is enough.
examples.analysis: 三两 = 150 grams. 就够了 'is enough': 就 makes the amount sound small. 不用那么多 'no need for that much' is what you tell a seller who is weighing out too much.

meaning: again (something has happened again); 又…又… 'both … and …'

senses.en: again, for a repeat that has already happened (a repeat still to come usually takes 再)
又 A 又 B: both A and B
(emphasis in a negative) after all, it's not as if: 我又不是医生

examples.en: It's raining again.
examples.analysis: 又 goes before the verb and means 'again' for a repeat that is already happening. 了 marks the new situation. For an 'again' that is still to come, Chinese usually uses 再: 明天再来.

examples.zh: 这家饭馆又便宜又好吃。
examples.en: This restaurant is both cheap and tasty.
examples.analysis: 又 A 又 B links two qualities, 'both A and B': 又便宜又好吃 'cheap and tasty'. The two parts usually point the same way, both good or both bad. 家 counts restaurants and shops.

examples.en: How come you forgot again?
examples.analysis: 怎么又 + verb + 了 is a common complaint: 'how come … again?'. 又 shows it has happened before, which is the whole point of the complaint.

related.en: again (a repeat still to come, or a request)

meaning: prefix before a surname: a friendly name for a younger person (小王)

senses.en: 小 + surname: a friendly way to address or mention someone younger, such as a junior colleague
小 + one syllable of a given name: a pet name for children or close friends (小明)

examples.en: Xiao Wang, come here a moment.
examples.analysis: 小 + surname is a common way for a senior colleague, or a peer of about the same age, to call someone younger or more junior: 小王 'young Wang'. It is friendly, not rude, but you would not use it for someone older or senior to you. 一下儿 'for a moment' softens the request.

examples.en: Xiao Li didn't come to work today.
examples.analysis: 小李 works as a name in the sentence, here the subject. People use these names when talking about colleagues, not only when calling them. 没来上班 'didn't come in to work'.

examples.en: Do you know Xiao Zhang?
examples.analysis: 小张 is the object of 认识 'be acquainted with'. The matching form is 老 + surname (老张), for someone older or a peer you have known a long time.

related.en: prefix: 老 + surname for someone older (老王)
small; young (the adjective; a separate entry)

meaning: should; it's time to; to be someone's turn

senses.en: should, ought to (shorter and more casual than 应该)
该 + verb + 了: it's time to …: 该走了
该 + person + 了: it's someone's turn: 该你了

examples.en: It's getting late. I should get going.
examples.analysis: 该 + verb + 了 = 'it's time (for me) to …'. 不早了 'it's no longer early' gives the reason. A standard way to start leaving a visit or a dinner.

examples.en: Your turn.
examples.analysis: 该 + person + 了 means 'it's your turn': in a game, a queue, or when someone has to speak or pay next. No verb is needed; the situation supplies it.

examples.en: What should I do?
examples.analysis: 该 here is 'should', placed before the question phrase 怎么办 'what to do'. 应该 works too; 该 is shorter and sounds more casual.

meaning: and so on; etc.; and others (ends a list)

senses.en: after a list: and others like these (often + a summing noun: 北京、上海等地方)
等等: 'and so on', the doubled form, common at the end of a spoken list

examples.zh: 我去过北京、上海等地方。
examples.en: I've been to Beijing, Shanghai and other places.
examples.analysis: 等 closes the list and means 'and others like these'. A noun after it, here 地方 'places', sums up what kind of things were listed. This pattern sounds a little more careful than chatty.

examples.zh: 他喜欢运动，比如打球、爬山等等。
examples.en: He likes sports, such as ball games, hiking and so on.
examples.analysis: 等等 is the doubled form, said like English 'and so on'. It ends the list on its own, with no noun after it, and is the more conversational choice. 比如 'for example' opens the list.

examples.zh: 别忘了带护照、钱包、手机等等。
examples.en: Don't forget to bring your passport, wallet, phone and so on.
examples.analysis: 等等 tells the listener the list is not complete: 'everything you need', not only these three. 别忘了 'don't forget' comes first, then 带 'take along' and the list.

related.en: to wait (the verb; a separate entry)

meaning: question; problem; issue

senses.en: a question (that you ask or answer)
a problem, trouble: 有问题 'something's wrong', 没问题 'no problem'

examples.zh: 我可以问你一个问题吗？
examples.en: Can I ask you a question?
examples.analysis: 问题 is the object here: 问 + 你 + 一个问题 'ask you a question'. 问 takes the person first, then the question, like English 'ask you something'.

examples.en: There seems to be something wrong with the computer.
examples.analysis: 有问题 'has a problem': 问题 means trouble here, not a question. 好像 'it seems' softens the claim. English says 'something is wrong with'; Chinese simply says the computer 有问题.

examples.en: If there's any problem, just call me.
examples.analysis: 有问题就… 'if there's a problem, then …': the condition needs no word for 'if'; 就 marks what follows from it. 给我打电话 'call me' is the request.

meaning: even more; more; still more

senses.en: even more (before an adjective): 更冷 'even colder'
more (before a verb of liking or wanting): 更喜欢 'prefer'

examples.en: Today is even colder than yesterday.
examples.analysis: A 比 B 更 + adjective: 更 adds 'even', which suggests yesterday was already cold. Without 更, 今天比昨天冷 just says 'colder'.

examples.en: I prefer tea.
examples.analysis: 更 + 喜欢 'like more, prefer', said when choosing between options. 更 goes before the verb, where English puts 'more' after it ('like tea more').

examples.en: Wouldn't it be better this way?
examples.analysis: 更好 'better (still)': the speaker suggests an improvement on the current plan. 是不是 before the comment asks for agreement, like English 'wouldn't it …?'.

meaning: to take or bring along; to take (someone) somewhere; to look after

senses.en: to take or bring with you: 带钱 'bring money'
to take or lead someone: 带你去 'take you there'
to look after (children): 带孩子

examples.en: Did you bring your passport?
examples.analysis: 带 + thing = 'have it with you, take it along'. 了吗 asks whether this has happened; the answer is 带了 'I did' or 没带 'I didn't'.

examples.en: I'll take you there.
examples.analysis: 带 + person + 去 'take someone there': the speaker goes along and leads the way. 吧 makes it a friendly offer.

examples.en: She stays at home looking after the kids.
examples.analysis: 带孩子 means 'look after the children', not just take them somewhere. 在家 'at home' comes before the verb and says where. A common way to describe a stay-at-home parent or grandparent.

related.en: to give; to see someone off; to deliver

meaning: time, occasion (counts how often something happens): 两回 'twice'

senses.en: time, occurrence: 去过两回 'have been twice'
这回 'this time', 下回 'next time'

examples.en: I've been there twice.
examples.analysis: Number + 回 counts how many times: 两回 'twice'. It comes after verb + 过, which marks experience. 次 means the same and is the neutral choice; 回 sounds more colloquial.

examples.en: This time it's on me.
examples.analysis: 这回 'this time' opens the sentence and sets the time frame. 请客 'treat, pay for others'. People often say it when taking turns paying, but the sentence itself does not say who paid before.

examples.en: How many times have I told you?
examples.analysis: 多少 + 回 asks 'how many times', but here it is a complaint, not a real question. The first 了 marks the saying as done; the last 了 counts up to now.

related.en: time, once through from start to finish
to return (the verb; a separate entry)

meaning: then; after that; and then

senses.en: then, after that: the next step in a sequence (often 先…然后…)
and then …: links events one after another when telling a story

examples.zh: 我们先吃饭，然后去看电影。
examples.en: We'll eat first, then go to a movie.
examples.analysis: 先…然后… 'first …, then …' sets out two steps in order. 然后 starts the second clause, and the subject 我们 is not repeated.

examples.en: And then what?
examples.analysis: 然后呢 asks a storyteller to go on: 'and then?'. 呢 makes it a follow-up question. It shows you are listening and want the rest of the story.

examples.zh: 到了先给我打电话，然后我去接你。
examples.en: When you arrive, call me first, and then I'll come and pick you up.
examples.analysis: 先…然后… again orders two steps, but each has its own doer: you call, then I come. 到了 'once (you've) arrived' opens the sentence with no word for 'when'.
